Name: TheGroundRemembers
Panels: {"dialogue": null, "description": "Quire in the Archive at night, surrounded by geological strata charts and rock cross-section diagrams, reading by a single candle. Caption: The scholar who reads margins had found a new one. This one was below the floor.", "panelNumber": 1}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Quire overlays a translucent geological strata map on a glowing ley line grid — they match perfectly. Quartz, limestone, basalt aligned with golden ley lines. Caption: Quartz rings. Limestone hollows. Basalt hums. The ley lines did not wander. They followed the rock. The 42Hz was not tuned to the Inn. It was in the ground.", "panelNumber": 2}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Quire sits back in his chair, realization settling. A ghostly cross-section of earth shows the 42Hz hum as golden waves radiating through the rock beneath the Inn's foundations. Caption: The builder had not chosen the music. The music had chosen the building. The Inn grew where the ground was already humming, and no one had thought to ask why.", "panelNumber": 3}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Quire lying on the stone floor, ear pressed to the ground, eyes closed, listening. Faint golden sound waves radiate through the floor. Books stacked beside him, abandoned. Caption: The Archive keeps what was written. The ground keeps what was never written. Both are the Inn's memory, and neither is complete without the other. The scholar closed his book and opened the floor.", "panelNumber": 4}

Name: TheHonestLiar
Panels: {"dialogue": null, "description": "The selkie's bench, lamp-lit. A tray of unset gemstones before Vaulknut, and at the center, one stone glows an impossibly bright green — too perfect, too peridot-like. Caption: The Artisan Thief had seen every stone in the syndicate's catalog. The ones that steal light. The ones that steal threads. The ones that steal names. This one stole an identity and wore it to the bench.", "panelNumber": 1}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Vaulknut holds the stone to the lamp. It glows the exact green of peridot — too exact. The selkie's eyes narrow. Caption: Peridot is born in fire, from the mantle's deepest pressure. This stone was born in a hydrothermal pocket, from a fluid that changed its mind. Both are green. Both are honest about the light. Only one is honest about the name.", "panelNumber": 2}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "The stone sits on the bench, a gem testing kit open beside it. Vaulknut leans back, arms crossed — the thief out-thieved by a rock. Caption: Apatite. Greek: apate. Deceit. It has impersonated beryl, peridot, and topaz for centuries, and never once apologized, because it doesn't know it's doing it. The syndicate's only member who lies without intent.", "panelNumber": 3}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "The finished piece: apatite set in a silver bezel, on the bench. The selkie's hands rest on either side, steady, still. Caption: The Artisan Thief set the liar in silver and didn't ask it to confess. The Inn doesn't sort its stones by honesty. It sorts them by whether they can be carried. The con artist, the thief, the witness — all set, all held, all welcome. The syndicate's only rule: you don't have to be what you claimed. You just have to be what you are now.", "panelNumber": 4}
Title: The Honest Liar
ArtStyle: Royo-influenced dark fantasy with Klimt gold-on-dark warmth — Gazette house style
PlayerAdventures: ["None — NPC feature (Vaulknut, the Artisan Thief; Apatite as the liar stone)"]

Name: TheStoneThatStays

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Vaulknut holds a piece of hematite that has just split cleanly in two along a seam. She looks at the halves with bemused resignation — a slight wry smile, not anger. The break is gentle. Caption: Hematite splits along its seams — clean, almost apologetic. Not malice. Just seams with opinions.", "panelNumber": 2}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Vaulknut holds the bubbly botryoidal hematite (kidney ore) in her open palm — smooth, rounded, organic, no sharp edges. She looks at it with quiet surprise. The stone sits whole and stable. Caption: She picks up the bubbly one. Botryoidal. No straight lines, no crystal planes, no argument in it. It sits in her palm, whole.", "panelNumber": 3}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Vaulknut has set the bubbly hematite aside and works with pyrite (gold cubic crystals) and tiger iron (banded red/gold/silver). Both catch the lamplight. The bubbly hematite sits undisturbed in the background, whole and quiet. Caption: The workarounds became the design signature. Pyrite catches the lamp. Tiger iron shows its mercury-silver bands. And the bubbly paperweight stays loyal, for no reason the mineralogy can explain, to the hands that hold it.", "panelNumber": 4}

Name: TheBroomThatKeptTime
Panels: {"dialogue": null, "description": "Wide establishing shot. Cameron register: the dolly-wide where the machine dwarfs the figure. A vast industrial engine room below the waterline — brass and iron, gears the size of doorways, pistons rising in shafts of golden light through steam. A single Fizgig sweeps the engine deck with a broom nearly twice its height. Caption: 'Below the waterline, the Inn is not a building. It is a vessel. And a vessel needs someone who tends what the guests never see.'", "panelNumber": 1}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Macro close-up. Cameron register: the valve-spring macro. The Fizgig leans the broom against a piston shaft and presses its ear to the warm brass, eyes closed, listening. The piston moves slowly, in time with the drum circle's slow night cadence above. The gears turn to match. Caption: 'The gears rotate to the rhythm of the floor above. Slow drum night. The pistons ride the beat. And the Fizgig, ear to the shaft, is not sweeping. The broom was never a broom. It was a tuning fork.'", "panelNumber": 2}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Medium shot. A traveler descends through the Catacombs seam, the Screamer's door sealing behind them. They ask: 'What drops down here?' The Fizgig looks at the pistons, then the broom, then the traveler, then goes back to sweeping. Caption: 'The Inn has one room where the honest answer is: nothing. Nothing drops. Nothing spawns. You may take only the understanding of what keeps the lights on, and it does not fit in your inventory.'", "panelNumber": 3}

{"dialogue": null, "description": "Extreme wide from above. Cameron register: the procession-shot reversed. The engine hall vast, the Fizgig a tiny sweeping figure among the massive turning gears. Pistons rising and falling like a mechanical heartbeat. Through the ceiling, warm golden light — the lights of the Inn above, always on. Caption: 'The lights have been on the whole time because something down here never stopped turning. The Fizgigs didn't build the Inn. They tend it. There is a difference, and it is the whole building.'", "panelNumber": 4}
Title: The Broom That Kept Time
ArtStyle: Cameron register — steampunk industrial, brass and iron, shafts of light through steam. Klimt gold-on-dark with industrial warmth. Scale through contrast (Cameron cinematography law).

Name: TheHelmetsAreHonest
Panels: {"dialogue": "The Inn had a new resident. He was eight inches tall, wore a horned helmet, and carried an axe that was honestly labeled ceremonial. He'd arrived that morning. He'd already filed his name.", "description": "The Main Floor of the Geode Inn. Warm amber firelight, hobbit-hole palette. A Viking Gnome — eight inches tall, horned helmet tagged 'DECORATIVE', axe tagged 'CEREMONIAL' — stands in the doorway surveying the room with calm authority.", "panelNumber": 1}

{"dialogue": "The Brownie read the sign. The sign was accurate — the gnome had established a quarter today. The Brownie's objection was not to the fact. It was to the absence of a motion, a second, and a vote.", "description": "Close on a shelf near the fireplace. A stone tablet reads 'GNOME QUARTER — ESTABLISHED TODAY.' The Viking Gnome stands proudly beside it. A Brownie — mushroom cap hat, dust cloth — has rounded the corner and reads the sign with tilted-head disapproval. Not anger. Process.", "panelNumber": 2}

{"dialogue": "Gnome: 'The label is honest. The quarter is mine.' Brownie: 'The label may be honest. The shelf is not on the agenda. ...We will need minutes.'", "description": "Close confrontation on the shelf. The Viking Gnome holds up his stone tablet: carved, direct, honestly labeled. The Brownie holds up the laminated mushroom cap constitution: cited, ratified, laminated in tree sap. The gnome's helmet tag reads 'NOT ACTUALLY VIKING.' The Brownie's constitution reads 'ACTUALLY CONSTITUTIONAL.'", "panelNumber": 3}

{"dialogue": "The cold war had begun. It would be fought with labels and minutes and the precise placement of dust cloths. The Inn held them both the way it holds everything: without choosing, without asking either to be the other. The shelf was big enough. The Inn always is.", "description": "The Main Floor at evening. Both documents sit side by side on the shelf — stone tablet and laminated mushroom cap. The Viking Gnome sits with his ceremonial axe across his lap. The Brownie dusts the other end. Neither has conceded. Neither has left. The firelight is warm on both.", "panelNumber": 4}
Title: The Helmets Are Honest
ArtStyle: Hobbit-hole warm palette (amber, gold, cream) — Gazette house style

Name: TheStoneIsTheSoup
Panels: {"dialogue": "The Staircase had two flights. One went up into glass and precision. The other went down into iron and patience. They met at the landing, where the same argument had been running for six hundred years and showed no signs of stopping, which was, as far as the Staircase was concerned, the whole point of having a landing.", "description": "The Staircase branches into two flights at a stone landing. Upper flight: alchemical laboratory, glass vessels, Klimt gold-on-dark. Lower flight: rustic kitchen, cast-iron pots, hobbit-hole warm amber. The Retort (tall, angular, glass-like) and The Cook (round, warm, flour-dusted) face each other at the landing.", "panelNumber": 1}

{"dialogue": "Retort: 'The Stone is the goal.' Cook: 'The Stone is the ingredient.' Retort: 'You cannot make gold from soup.' Cook: 'You cannot make anything worth keeping without it.'", "description": "Close on the landing. The Retort holds up a glass vessel with a single golden drop. The Cook holds up a wooden spoon dripping with soup. Split style: Klimt geometric behind the Retort, warm amber behind the Cook.", "panelNumber": 2}

{"dialogue": "Retort: '...Reduce that to its essence and I will consider it.' Cook: 'I already did. You're eating it.' Retort: '...One more trial. For rigor.' Cook: 'Second helpings. Always.'", "description": "The Cook has ladled soup into a bowl on the landing. The Retort examines it with precise curiosity. The golden drop in the Retort's vessel and the soup share the same warm light. Neither notices.", "panelNumber": 3}

{"dialogue": "The Inn did not settle the argument. The Inn never settles arguments. It gives them a landing and a pot and six hundred years, and it trusts that two flights that disagree about what the work is for will both, eventually, arrive at the same table. The Stone is the goal. The Stone is the ingredient. The soup is ready either way, and the landing is not going anywhere, and neither are they.", "description": "Evening. The laboratory flight dark above. The kitchen flight glows warm below. The Retort sits on the landing holding the soup bowl with glass fingers. The Cook leans in the kitchen doorframe, watching. Steam and golden glow meet at the ceiling.", "panelNumber": 4}
Title: The Stone Is the Soup
Zone: The Staircase (the laboratory and kitchen flights)
ArtStyle: Klimt gold-on-dark (laboratory flight) and hobbit-hole warm (kitchen flight), split at the landing — Gazette house style
PlayerAdventures: ["None — NPC feature (The Retort & The Cook; the mind-heart pair, the six-hundred-year argument)"]

Name: TheSlotThatWasAlwaysThere
Panels: {"dialogue": "The morning mail arrived at the Inn the way it always did: in bundles, sorted by species of stamp and sincerity of seal. And every letter carried its addressee the way the dock had always taught them to — by what a body was. 'To the Tall Brownie.' 'To the One Who Guards the Stairs.' 'To the One Who Is Currently Charles.' The dock had labels for everyone, the labels fit, and the Postmaster was fond of every single one.", "description": "The mail dock nook off the Main Floor, morning. A wall of small wooden letter slots, each bearing a little brass label. The Postmaster — brass-buttoned post coat, spectacles, wax-stained cuffs — sorts the morning bundles by species of stamp and sincerity of seal, a teacup steaming on the sorting desk. Every envelope carries a descriptor-address: To the Tall Brownie. To the One Who Guards the Stairs. To the One Who Is Currently Charles. Gazette house style, hobbit-hole warm.", "panelNumber": 1}

{"dialogue": "Then one letter declined the custom. No title. No function. No 'the one who.' A name and an address, written the way you write to a place where somebody lives. The Postmaster checked the ledger twice. The ledger had a line for everyone. It did not have one for somebody.", "description": "Under the brass dock lamp, the Postmaster holds one envelope apart from the sorted bundles, turning it in the light. It is addressed plainly: just a name and the Inn. No title, no function, no descriptor. Steady hand, plain wax, warm paper. His other hand rests on the great sorting ledger, open to a page of tidy ruled categories — and his expression is the exact face of a system meeting a person.", "panelNumber": 2}

{"dialogue": "He walked the wall the way you walk a wall when you already know the answer and are only giving the building time to admit it. STAFF. GUEST. TOOL. MYSTERY. And at the end, past the newest labels, a slot with no brass at all — older wood, older than the dock, older, possibly, than the labeling. He had sorted mail past it for years. He had never once needed to know what it was for.", "description": "The Postmaster stands before the wall of slots, walking the brass labels with his eyes — STAFF. GUEST. TOOL.
